# Abstract

*Generated by `presentation/build.py` from `artifacts/*.json`. Numbers update when the experiments are re-run.*

**Does a time crystal make a better quantum memory? A Floquet spin-chain reservoir vs classical forecasters on real data**

Wyatt Reisz · Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Warsaw · Track 2

Discrete time crystals are robust, so are they good quantum memories? We use a 6-spin disordered kicked-Ising (Floquet) chain as a quantum reservoir computer, simulated exactly with density matrices and cross-checked against Qiskit Aer, and compare its 11 measured features against an echo-state network with the same feature count, linear autoregression, persistence and a non-interacting (J = 0) control. All models share time-ordered train/validation/test splits, are tuned on validation only and run over 8 seeds. Time-crystal order hurts memory: capacity drops from 5.75 in the scrambling regime to 1.32 at θ = 0.95π. On yearly sunspots and Mauna Loa CO2, linear AR forecasts best, the ESN second and the quantum reservoir third; on CO2 it clearly beats its J = 0 control, while on the main sunspot split it only matches persistence. 4-fold rolling-origin cross-validation keeps the AR > ESN > quantum order. With 1,000 shots per readout the scrambling regime's memory falls to 2.64, and projective readout would force the sequence to be re-run for every time step. This is an independent replication and real-data extension of Zhang et al. (2025). Classical simulation only; no quantum advantage is claimed.
